riskTone.label: BEARISH
riskTone.rationale: Iran escalating strikes on US bases signals geopolitical risk-off; higher-for-longer rate fears add hawkish headwind, both bearish for UK100.

briefing.briefing: Starting with sterling (the most important signal for FTSE 100): GBPUSD is down just -0.12% today, which by the index's inverted relationship with the pound (weaker pound makes the overseas earnings of UK multinationals worth more in sterling terms) is a mild tailwind for UK100 — but the snapshot rates this as effectively NEUTRAL given how small the move is. The dominant forces today are pulling in opposite directions, which explains the messy, directionless picture: on the bullish side, Brent crude is surging +3.37%, directly lifting Shell and BP (top-5 index weights), and copper is up +0.66%, giving miners a gentle nudge; on the bearish side, US equities are soft (S&P 500 -0.36%, Nasdaq -1.51%), VIX [a measure of how nervous US markets are] sits at 17.08 in an ELEVATED regime meaning caution is warranted, and professional futures traders are heavily 'crowded short' [meaning a lot of big money is already betting against the pound, which the snapshot reads as a bearish signal for FTSE]. The biggest headline from the last few hours (4.1 hours ago, Reuters) is that Iran has escalated strikes on US bases — a classic geopolitical risk-off event [meaning investors tend to avoid risky assets and move to safety] that is keeping sentiment cautious and directly explains why gold is falling (-2.06%, as a 'higher-for-longer rates' narrative competes with the safe-haven bid) and why UK100 is slightly negative on the day (-0.29%). The 20-year gilt yield is actually falling 5bp today (long-end stress flag is false), so there is no UK fiscal-crisis signal to worry about. Directional bias is CHOPPY/NEUTRAL: energy is pulling the index up, geopolitics and weak US markets are pulling it down, and there is no clean dominant force. Confidence is 4/10 — the geopolitical situation could deteriorate rapidly (bearish) or de-escalate (bullish), and AstraZeneca (often the single largest index weight) carries idiosyncratic risk that could swing the index independently of everything else. For the 08:00 ORB trade specifically: the opening range (ORB high 10,526 / ORB low 10,482, a 44-point range) has so far produced NO breakout in either direction ('NONE'), which combined with the tug-of-war between energy bulls and geopolitical bears strongly suggests a fakeout/chop day rather than a clean trend breakout — traders should be very cautious about chasing moves and should wait for a confirmed break with follow-through. Roughly 62% of the 14-day average daily range [the typical distance the index travels in a day, here 133 points] has already been used, meaning there are about 50 points of 'budget' left, so large trending moves are less likely from here. No scheduled UK economic events fall today, but traders must note a HIGH-impact UK GDP Monthly Estimate (a measure of how fast the economy grew) is due on Thursday 16 July at 07:00 BST — just before the London open — so position sizing later this week should be reduced ahead of that release. Key levels: overnight high 10,526 and ORB high 10,526 are the same level and act as the upside line in the sand; overnight low 10,443 and ORB low 10,482 define the downside; prior day high 10,537 is just above and prior day low 10,439 just below as wider reference points. The one thing to remember today: energy is the bull, geopolitics is the bear, and with no ORB break yet and 62% of the daily range already used, the smart play is to wait for a decisive move rather than force a trade.
